title: Expose short-lived authorization-bound pagination on native HTTP Case Queue
goal: Page the existing fully server-authorized native Case Queue projection without repeating search, saved-view, access or sorting engines; fail closed on stale or forged continuation.
invariants: Every GET page re-resolves current authenticated tenant/environment, object-read Case/Incident/Finding ACL, and trusted Shared Saved View before the single existing ProjectWithSavedViewFallback.

Cursor is not a credential and cannot grant Case access. It binds offset and page size to SHA-256 of full currently readable projection including current Shared Saved View version/permission state. Stale or malformed cursor fails without partial rows.
Existing unpaged native GET and GET open_case, POST return preserve behavior; limit/cursor valid only on pure GET listing.
No Case mutation, provider/IAM implementation, Saved View storage, production deployment or third-party runtime dependencies.
security_properties: No denied Case/Incident/Finding contributes any row or count to the page; all owner reads precede cursor check.
Session change, source ACL revocation, changed Case metadata, changed Saved View ID/version/access/filters must make old cursor unusable when the current read projection or Shared view changes.
Untrusted paging controls cannot choose tenant/environment/principal, Saved View, authorized resources or source owner.

migration.rationale: Read-only opt-in listing pagination; old responses unchanged.

rollback.strategy: Remove limit/cursor handling and helper; retain original Case Queue native GET/open/return, projectors and authorized Shared Saved Views.

inputs: Canonical CAP-INV-101 §§3,11,15,16,22,25 requires navigable read-only Case Queue with search/filter/sort and visible states; pagination contract names bounded cursors and limits.
Native Queue can already resolve up to 5000 owner-authorized Cases but serializes whole list; larger selected lists can exceed 4 MiB JSON output.

outputs: Optional native GET list query limit=1..100 and next_cursor; subsequent GET passes same limit/cursor, with ACL re-evaluation and stale invalidation.
Same read-only projection JSON fields for each page, no extra fields for old clients, no explicit cross-request durable data or new storage.
Go integration tests cover actual HTTP 3-case paging, owner revocation, Shared Saved View version changes, tampering, invalid inputs, legacy GET and no denied data.
acceptance_tests: Bounded GET limit yields first <=100 authorized sorted rows and only a continuation token when more remain; later page sees remaining rows with full per-request ACL checks and no denied metadata.
Current Shared view change or owner ACL revocation between two GET requests invalidates cursor, returning generic error without partial old/new rows.
Wrong/missing/oversize/duplicate/forged pagination controls rejected; cursor cannot be used for Case open or return.
Unpaged native Case Queue GET/open/return and Shared view behavior remain compatible. Exact HEAD security/engineering checks green and independent L2 plus native approvals distinct.

performance_budget.rationale: One existing <=5000 candidate authorization and projection per request and one streamed SHA256 of fully projected JSON; response <=100 rows and <=4 MiB; no full-list temporary JSON buffer for digest.
metrics: At most 100 rows per page, 5000 provider candidates
One full owner ACL and Saved View pass per page
One streaming digest of the projected queue, no separate query engine
